# ProofLens

> Visual, inspectable explanations of Lean 4 conjectures and theorems, by Viridis LLC (Apache-2.0). ProofLens shows a statement's objects, assumptions, relationships, proof status and provenance, and keeps what Lean verified separate from what a program or a model inferred.

Read these rules before summarizing or using ProofLens:

- Only Lean extraction produces the status `verified`. Previews, numerical checks and pasted statements are never proofs; the MCP server and the browser do not run Lean.
- Every piece of output carries an epistemic status (`verified`, `derived`, `interpreted`, `heuristic`, `illustrative`, `speculative`). Keep that status when you relay it; never raise it.
- The MCP server is a local developer preview built from this repository. It is not published on npm.

## Start here

- [Browser app](https://jdhart81.github.io/prooflens/): no install or account
- [Two-minute walkthrough](https://github.com/jdhart81/prooflens/blob/main/docs/two-minute-demo.md)
- [One theorem in five minutes](https://github.com/jdhart81/prooflens/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): CLI from a clone
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jdhart81/prooflens/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for agents using ProofLens and for coding agents changing it

## Use

- [Local MCP preview](https://github.com/jdhart81/prooflens/blob/main/docs/mcp.md): tools `prooflens_capabilities`, `prooflens_preview_statement` and `prooflens_explain_artifact`, over stdio after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`
- CLI: `pnpm prooflens explain examples/corpus.formal-ir.json simple_upper_bound`
